title: Acetylcholine demixes heterogeneous dopamine signals for learning and moving
goal: Surpass the source-paper result on the same task: Candidate ordered source subtask is Figure 6g–h: predict whether contralateral reaction time is in the fastest or slowest within-session quartile from simultaneously recorded DMS spiking. This is explicitly a scoped paper subtask; Figure 3 timing and the paper’s full causal demixing claims remain distinct obligations, not silently replaced or won.
primary_outputs: Candidate method and outputs for the source task: Candidate ordered source subtask is Figure 6g–h: predict whether contralateral reaction time is in the fastest or slowest within-session quartile from simultaneously recorded DMS spiking. This is explicitly a scoped paper subtask; Figure 3 timing and the paper’s full causal demixing claims remain distinct obligations, not silently replaced or won.

Source-paper comparison for Figure 6h mean within-session cross-validated fast/slow reaction-time classification accuracy (%): Per-session cross-validated classification accuracy in percent: 100 times one minus the minimum kfoldLoss among the 11 ridge penalties. It is a source selection-biased CV statistic, not an independent external test accuracy.
success_criteria: Explicitly bind the improvement objective to the original Figure 6 reaction-time decoder without claiming the full demixing mechanism or dropping historical timing obligations.
Recover the original full 18-session/eight-rat manifest, published numeric accuracy and fold/penalty-selection realization; qualify an author baseline after documenting any source-code correction.
Use the identical original spike window, contralateral rule, reaction-time quartiles and qualifying sessions; new rat splits or reduced sessions cannot count as the same-task paper win.
Freeze candidate, concrete access/resource budgets, meaningful effect and dependence-aware uncertainty before final comparison.
Latency reconstruction agreement, larger DA/ACh phase separation and stronger biological significance do not count as predictive improvement.
The bound improvement contract must be improvement_ready and its complete same-task comparison and admission requirements must pass.
Reproduction is calibration only; reconstructing a numerical result, changing the task or split, or achieving stronger significance alone is not success.
